thread.title: Why QUALCOMM, Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) shares surged 4.83% in after-hours?

author: Daniel Stone
title: Why QUALCOMM, Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) shares surged 4.83% in after-hours?
text:
March 15, 2018 Why QUALCOMM, Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM) shares surged 4.83% in after-hours? 
QUALCOMM, Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM ) shares advances 4.83% in extended session on Thursday following the news on Thursday that Broadcom said it was likely to pursue the smaller acquisitions of chip-makers, after its failed hostile takeover bid to acquire rival Qualcomm Inc (QCOM). The company said that its smart phone chip business would see an an increase from South Korea, and a decline in demand this quarter from a North American customer. 
The North American customer of Broadcom is Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL), most analysts believe that, which made up a fifth of the company revenue last year, and Samsung Electronics is the Korean customer of Broadcom, which is ramping up the production of its recently announced Galaxy S9 smart phone. 
The quarterly results of Broadcom beat the analysts expectations, days after Donald Trump blocked its $117 billion hostile bid for QCOM merely based on the national security concerns. Singapore-based Broadcom, scrapped the offer on Wednesday. 
“Typically, Broadcom has to make acquisitions to drive the earnings,” said Summit Insight Group analyst Kinngai Chan. “If the company is able to make two or three medium-size acquisitions, then I think the stock will move up again.” 
“Qualcomm was clearly a unique and very large acquisition opportunity,” Chief Financial Officer Tom Krause told investors on a conference call. “Given the maturity of the industry, the consolidation it is seeing and our relative size now, our future acquisitions are much more likely to be funded with cash available on our balance sheet and without the need to flex the balance sheet.” 
But Broadcom officials were still publicly smarting over the loss of the Qualcomm deal. Krause said he was “touched” by an Institutional Shareholder Services report Wednesday encouraging Qualcomm shareholders to cast protest ballots for Broadcom’s director nominees. 
Krause said Broadcom believes that “based on the vote tally as of today, the 11 Qualcomm nominees are only garnering between 15 percent to 16 percent of the outstanding shares, not necessarily something to celebrate on San Diego.” Qualcomm declined to comment on Krause’s comments.
